decisive_item.title: Can Micron Technology Become the New Nvidia?
decisive_item.passage: tight market conditions could last until 2028

meaning.what: memory market stays tight: demand above supply, prices sharply higher, new industry capacity not online until 2027 or later

kept_from_that_article.summary: Micron Technology said in its latest quarterly announcement that tight memory market conditions could last until 2028, according to Fool.com's report; Micron gave no size for the shortage beyond the 2028 date.
passages: Micron recently announced another jaw-dropping quarter with huge growth and incredible expectations for the following quarter, dropping huge news that tight market conditions could last until 2028.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Fool.com's Keithen Drury forecast that new memory-industry capacity will not be online until 2027 or later, leaving low inventory and hence low supply for at least the next year and a half, which could push memory chip prices even higher because demand is not slowing.
passages: As mentioned, new capacity for many in this industry won't be online until 2027 or later, creating a low supply of inventory for at least the next year and a half. That could lead to even higher memory chip prices, as demand for these devices isn't slowing down.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Fool.com reported that the AI hyperscalers plan to spend $650 billion on data-center capital expenditures this year (2026) and that next year the figure could be over $1 trillion, which the article says will raise demand for memory chips as well as for NVIDIA GPUs.
passages: While the AI hyperscalers plan to spend $650 billion on data center capital expenditures this year, next year that figure could be over $1 trillion. That will lead to even higher demand for memory chips, as well as for Nvidia GPUs.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Micron Technology guided revenue for its next quarter to $50 billion, which Fool.com said is about half of what NVIDIA is expected to generate in the comparable period; Micron gave the $50 billion guidance without specifying NVIDIA's expected figure.
passages: Next quarter, it expects $50 billion in revenue, or about half of what Nvidia is expected to generate.

decisive_item.title: China to let AI firms buy Nvidia H200s, says report
decisive_item.who: The Information, citing two unidentified people (via Bloomberg / Straits Times)
decisive_item.passage: China plans to allow top artificial intelligence companies to buy a limited amount of H200 chips from Nvidia

meaning.what: permission for top AI companies (Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek) to buy NVIDIA H200 chips, each on approval stating the number and reason
meaning.how_much: a limited amount; total may be fewer than 200,000

kept_from_that_article.summary: The Information reported on July 8, 2026, citing two unidentified people familiar with the matter, that China plans to allow top AI companies including Alibaba Group, ByteDance and DeepSeek to buy a limited amount of NVIDIA H200 AI chips, easing previous restrictions. Chinese officials informed the companies they will have permission to purchase some processors; companies must specify how many chips they need and why to get approval, and the total may end up below 200,000 chips.
passages: China plans to allow top artificial intelligence companies to buy a limited amount of H200 chips from Nvidia, a sign the country is easing restrictions on the coveted US technology, according to the Information news site.

Chinese officials have informed companies such as Alibaba Group, ByteDance and DeepSeek that they will have permission to purchase some of the processors, which are used to develop AI models, the news site said on July 8 .
The companies need to say how many chips they need – and why – to get approval, according to the Information.
The Chinese government, meanwhile, is still figuring out how many H200 chips to allow the companies to buy, but the total may end up being fewer than 200,000, the Information reported.
But soaring demand for AI processors helped spur the Chinese authorities to allow some H200 purchases, according to the Information, citing two unidentified people familiar with the matter.

kept_from_that_article.summary: NVIDIA Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress said in May 2026 that the H200 chips had not generated any revenue for NVIDIA in China and that NVIDIA was uncertain whether any imports would be allowed into the country.
passages: In May, Nvidia chief financial officer Colette Kress said the H200 chips had yet to generate any revenue for the company in China.
“We are uncertain whether any imports will be allowed into the country,” she said.

kept_from_that_article.summary: NVIDIA is working to release its more powerful Rubin AI chip line-up in the second half of calendar 2026, the article reports.
passages: Nvidia is now working to release an even more powerful line-up called Rubin in the second half of 2026 .

kept_from_that_article.summary: Washington has continued to restrict sales to China of more capable AI chips than the H200 on national security grounds, the article reports.
passages: Washington has continued to restrict sales of more capable AI chips to China on national security grounds.

kept_from_that_article.summary: US President Donald Trump granted NVIDIA permission in December to sell the H200 processors to China, although Chinese authorities had been slow to allow the technology into the country, the article reports.
passages: Though US President Donald Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell the processors to China in December, the Chinese authorities have been slow to allow the technology into the country.

decisive_item.title: Nvidia slashes list of authorized customers in Asia in a bid to reduce AI chip smuggling, report claims — company sent field inspectors, called customers to check if business is genuine after pressure from Washington
decisive_item.passage: Beijing refused to allow Chinese companies to buy these AI processors

meaning.what: Chinese companies not allowed to buy NVIDIA H200

kept_from_that_article.summary: NVIDIA has reportedly created a new 'whitelist' of verified customers in Asia, cutting its number of authorized clients by more than half; remaining customers passed tougher compliance inspections — field staff visits to customer data centers, contract verification and end-user interviews — to screen out shell companies that forward NVIDIA GPUs and servers into China. Sources told the Financial Times the move followed pressure from Washington to tighten legal compliance. NVIDIA did not immediately comment.
passages: AI tech giant Nvidia, which builds some of the most coveted AI chips in the world, has reportedly created a new “whitelist” of verified companies to help prevent its products from getting smuggled into China. According to the Financial Times , this roster cuts the number of authorized clients by more than half, with those remaining having passed tougher compliance inspections to ensure that they are genuine businesses, not shell companies designed to forward Nvidia GPUs and servers into China. Some of the steps that Nvidia took to help safeguard its chips reportedly included sending staff to customer data centers, contract verification, and interviewing end users.

Sources told the publication that the company made this move after Washington pressured it into tightening its legal compliance, which comes months after the arrest of Supermicro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw , alongside two other suspects, for allegedly smuggling $2.5 billion worth of Nvidia hardware into China.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Beijing has refused to allow Chinese companies to buy NVIDIA's U.S.-approved AI processors (H200 GPUs), instead relying on domestic semiconductor manufacturers to make up the compute shortfall — a policy that bars the China sales Washington cleared, with domestic supply 'apparently still not enough.'
passages: However, Beijing refused to allow Chinese companies to buy these AI processors — instead, it’s banking on domestic semiconductor manufacturers to make up for the shortfall, but it’s apparently still not enough.

kept_from_that_article.summary: In December 2025, President Donald Trump reversed U.S. policy and allowed NVIDIA to export its H200 GPUs to select customers in China/Asia, a step that would have eased the region's AI-chip shortage.
passages: President Donald Trump took a 180-degree turn in December 2025 and finally allowed Nvidia to export its H200 GPUs to select customers in the region, which would have alleviated the situation.

kept_from_that_article.summary: An unnamed tech executive told the Financial Times that all Chinese domestic AI-chip suppliers are sold out, and Chinese buyers are even considering less powerful chips as long as they can be put to use — indicating unserved AI compute demand in China amid constrained supply.
passages: One tech executive even told the Financial Times that all domestic suppliers are sold out and that they’re even considering less powerful chips, as long as they could be put to use.

decisive_item.title: Nvidia GPU Debt Backstop Unleashes the AI Project Trinity: Capital, Offtake and Datacenters
decisive_item.who: Sharon AI (counterparty disclosure, reported by SemiAnalysis)
decisive_item.passage: Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B

meaning.what: total value of NVIDIA's backstop on Sharon's 72MW Australian AI factory (up to 40,000 GB300)

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reports that NVIDIA has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes itself: under the backstop program NVIDIA gives Neoclouds a take-or-pay commitment — a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity — and in exchange shares in a portion of the Neocloud's revenue earned above the backstop level. Backstop programs are typically six years, during which NVIDIA stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over time.
passages: This is why Nvidia has stepped in and has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes themselves . In the backstop program, Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment to Neoclouds – a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity. In exchange for this backstop, Nvidia also shares in a portion of the Neocloud’s revenue earned above the backstop level.
Nvidia’s backstop program is typically six years in length, and during these six years, Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over the time period.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reports that NVIDIA has gone deeper than GPU-rental backstops and has started backstopping datacenter leases for Neoclouds, adding a further layer of credit support.
passages: Here, Nvidia is diving even deeper, as it has started backstopping datacenter leases.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis presents an illustrative NVIDIA backstop pricing curve averaging about $2.36/hr over the six-year period, which it believes is at the lower end of the expected backstop range and expects most Neoclouds to negotiate higher backstops. In its modeled short-tenor scenario the NVIDIA revenue-share take rate works out to about 18% on average over six years.
passages: the below table is an illustrative example to explain the basic terms of the program – we present a backstop pricing curve that we believe to be on the lower end of the backstop range – in this case at an average of $2.36 over the six-year period, but we expect that most Neoclouds will negotiate higher backstops.
Over the six years of this scenario, the Nvidia take rate works out to be about 18% on average, but without the backstop, there would be no cluster!

kept_from_that_article.summary: SharonAI's 72MW AI factory in Australia, announced in June 2026, scales to as many as 40,000 GB300s under a six-year NVIDIA backstop; Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B, an implied floor of about $2.33/hr/GPU on average over the six years. Sharon's footprint is set to grow to 132MW with 102MW contracted, and it guides to reaching more than 55,000 NVIDIA GPUs in total (including the 40,000 backstopped GB300s) by mid-2027.
passages: The first is SharonAI’s 72MW AI factory in Australia. Announced in June 2026, the deal has SharonAI scaling up to as many as 40,000 GB300s under a six-year backstop. Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B, which works out to an implied floor of about $2.33/hr/GPU on average over the six year period.

Sharon AI’s footprint is now set to grow to 132MW with 102MW contracted, and the company guides to reaching more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs in total (inclusive of the 40,000 GB300s backstopped) by mid-2027.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Firmus's 360MW AI cluster in Batam, Indonesia, announced June 29, 2026, is the next major project announced with an NVIDIA backstop. Firmus announced it expects $25B to $30B of customer revenue over the six years, and SemiAnalysis expects a portion of revenue above the backstop level will be shared with NVIDIA.
passages: Firmus’s 360MW AI Cluster in Batam, Indonesia is the next major project announced with an Nvidia backstop.
Announced just recently on June 29 th , 2026, this project shows the scale at which Nvidia is rolling out the backstop program.

Firmus announced that they expect $25B to $30B of customer revenue over the six years. We expect a portion of the revenue above the backstop level will be shared with Nvidia as per the structure we outlined earlier today.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis estimates that the broader market remains materially lower on NVIDIA shipment volumes and revenue estimates for the second half of 2026 than its own supply-chain-based Accelerator Model tracking implies.
passages: Nvidia revenue is skyrocketing, and even 3 years into the build out, the general market is still materially lower on shipment volumes and revenue estimates for Nvidia in the 2nd half of this year versus our through supply chain tracking in the Accelerator Model .

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis notes AMD has already been providing GPU backstops starting last year; per its June 2025 AMD article, AMD offered AWS, OCI, Digital Ocean, Vultr, Tensorwave, Crusoe and other Neoclouds a backstop deal in which, in exchange for buying more AMD GPUs, AMD would stand ready to rent back a significant chunk of the capacity on long-term contracts for internal AMD software development if the Neocloud could not fully sell it.
passages: Nvidia is not the only merchant GPU vendor to utilize backstops. AMD has already been providing backstops starting last year. We wrote in our AMD article from June 2025 that AMD offered AWS, OCI, Digital Ocean, Vultr, Tensorwave, Crusoe and other Neoclouds a backstop deal, whereby in exchange for customers’ willingness to buy more AMD GPUs, AMD will stand ready to rent back a significant chunk of this capacity in the form of long-term contracts for internal AMD software development purposes if the Neocloud isn’t able to full sell their capacity.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis forecasts annual AI capex — including GPUs, networking, storage, attached CPU compute and the datacenters to house it — will be well north of $2T in 2028, with cumulative AI capex from 2024 to 2029 reaching about $11.1T, and credit markets the main funding source.
passages: Annual AI Capex – including GPUs, networking, storage and attached CPU compute as well as for the Datacenters to house AI compute – will be well north of $2T in 2028. Cumulative AI Capex from 2024 to 2029 will reach ~$11.1T, and credit markets will be the main funding source for this buildout.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis forecasts AI debt financing will become a multi-trillion-dollar credit market with over $7T of debt outstanding by 2029, driven by AI IT capex and AI datacenter capex needs of Neoclouds, datacenter builders and even hyperscalers, making it the second-largest asset-backed debt market after the roughly $13T US mortgage-backed market.
passages: AI Debt Financing will become a multi-trillion-dollar credit market, with over $7T of debt outstanding by 2029 driven both by AI IT Capex and AI Datacenter Capex needs for Neoclouds, datacenter builders, and even hyperscalers. This will make it the second largest asset backed debt market after the US mortgage-backed financing market at just over $13T.

kept_from_that_article.summary: On July 1, The Information reported that NVIDIA is providing financial guarantees to young GPU cloud providers: if these companies fail to secure enough AI developers to rent their capacity, NVIDIA will repurchase their unsold GPU capacity at a pre-agreed price. In return NVIDIA receives a percentage of the providers' revenue, with the revenue-sharing rate declining over the contract term. GPU cloud providers Firmus and Sharon AI have joined the program, and three executives with existing ties to NVIDIA confirmed the arrangement.
passages: On July 1, according to the technology news outlet The Information, NVIDIA is providing financial guarantees to young cloud service providers that lease or rent its GPUs—if these companies fail to secure enough AI developers to rent their computing capacity, NVIDIA will repurchase their unsold GPU capacity at a pre-agreed price.

In return, NVIDIA will receive a percentage of these cloud providers’ revenue, with the revenue-sharing rate gradually declining over the term of the contract. GPU cloud providers Firmus and Sharon AI have already joined the program, and three executives with existing business ties to NVIDIA confirmed the arrangement.

kept_from_that_article.summary: On July 1, NVIDIA published a statement on its official website announcing a new business model combining revenue sharing with credit support, enabling AI cloud providers to procure NVIDIA infrastructure without bearing the full upfront capital expenditure and to offer computing services to downstream AI-native enterprises, model developers and corporate clients. Per NVIDIA's press release, the company will earn not only standard product revenue but also an additional share of cloud service revenue, creating a usage-based recurring revenue stream.

According to NVIDIA’s official press release, the company will earn not only standard product revenue but also an additional share of cloud service revenue, creating a usage-based, recurring revenue stream.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reports that NVIDIA has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes itself: under the backstop program NVIDIA gives Neoclouds a take-or-pay commitment — a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity — and in exchange shares in a portion of the Neocloud's revenue earned above the backstop level. Backstop programs are typically six years, during which NVIDIA stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over time.
passages: This is why Nvidia has stepped in and has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes themselves . In the backstop program, Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment to Neoclouds – a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity. In exchange for this backstop, Nvidia also shares in a portion of the Neocloud’s revenue earned above the backstop level.
Nvidia’s backstop program is typically six years in length, and during these six years, Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over the time period.
